The controller shall start the automatic fill-transfer-drain sequence upon a valid START command when the process is idle or paused.
The automatic sequence shall open inlet valve V1 to fill Tank 1.
After Tank 1 reaches the high-level limit, the controller shall wait 10 s before opening V2.
V2 shall transfer liquid from Tank 1 to Tank 2 until Tank 1 reaches its low-level limit.
After Tank 1 reaches the low-level limit, the controller shall wait 10 s before opening V3.
V3 shall drain Tank 2 until Tank 2 reaches its low-level limit.
After Tank 2 reaches its low-level limit, the controller shall return to the Tank 1 filling operation after 10 s.
STOP shall close V1, V2 and V3 and place the controller in a paused condition.
A START command following STOP shall continue the sequence from the point at which STOP was accepted.
SHUT shall command V2 and V3 open to drain both tanks and shall inhibit V1.
After shutdown draining is complete, all three valves shall be closed and the controller shall be in the initial idle configuration.
On loss of controller power, all process valves shall move to or remain in the closed position.
SHUT shall have higher command priority than STOP; STOP shall have higher priority than START.
V1 shall never be commanded open while V2 is open.
During normal automatic operation, V2 and V3 shall not be open simultaneously.
During SHUT mode, V2 and V3 may be open simultaneously.
Tank 1 high-level setpoint shall be 0.80 m.
Tank 1 low-level setpoint shall be 0.05 m.
Tank 2 low-level setpoint shall be 0.05 m.
The post-transfer waiting time shall be 12 s.
The inter-cycle waiting time after Tank 2 reaches low level shall be 8 s.
The controller shall receive two analog level measurements designated LT-101 and LT-102.
The controller shall receive momentary START, STOP and SHUT digital commands.
The controller shall provide three discrete valve-open commands to XV-101, XV-102 and XV-103.
A STOP command received during a wait state shall freeze the wait timer rather than restart it.
START commands received while already running shall be ignored.
STOP commands received during SHUT mode shall be ignored until shutdown is complete.
START commands received during SHUT mode shall be ignored until shutdown is complete.
Shutdown completion shall require Tank 1 and Tank 2 to both be at or below their low-level setpoints.
The demonstration run shall simulate from 0 s through 900 s.
The demonstration run shall apply START at 20 s, STOP at 220 s, START at 280 s, STOP at 650 s and SHUT at 700 s.

CONTROL LOGIC DESIGN NOTE
Two-Tank Fill/Transfer/Drain Controller

This note defines the controller state semantics and resolves command-priority questions raised against URS-001 Rev A. It does not replace the mechanical model or supplier data. Numeric setpoints and delays shall follow the latest approved parameter/change records.

Legacy simulation code uses states FILL, HOLD1, TRANSFER, HOLD2, DRAIN and HOLD3. These map to FILL_T1, WAIT_AFTER_FILL, TRANSFER_T1_T2, WAIT_AFTER_TRANSFER, DRAIN_T2 and WAIT_AFTER_DRAIN respectively. The old code has no explicit PAUSED state object and handles STOP with a Boolean latch.

Commands received while SHUTDOWN is active do not interrupt the shutdown sequence. A new START is required after shutdown has completed and the controller has returned to IDLE.
The V2/V3 simultaneous-open restriction is explicitly waived in SHUTDOWN.

The URS says STOP waits for either START or SHUT but does not state what happens to an active delay timer. Controls proposed freezing remaining delay. Simulation initially restarted the entire delay on resume. The review board selected **freeze remaining delay** because STOP should pause the process rather than alter the sequence timing.

- **D-01:** Command precedence is `SHUT > STOP > START`.
- **D-02:** STOP closes all valves and stores the interrupted state.
- **D-03:** STOP during any delay freezes the remaining delay; START resumes the remaining delay.
- **D-04:** START while the automatic sequence is already running is ignored.
- **D-05:** START and STOP received during active SHUT are ignored.
- **D-06:** SHUT is complete only when both LT-101 and LT-102 are at or below their low-level setpoints.
- **D-07:** After shutdow
